System One delegation architecture (5-10x token savings via cheap specialist models) is the kind of architecture we dream about. Offload classification/verification/guard to dedicated pipeline.
Deskbar replicant is solid — BArchivable, HVIF icon, proper popup menu. BFS-queryable sessions via extended attributes is console-level platform-deep thinking.

veteran_wisdom: "We shipped a coding agent in 2021. The single biggest regret: synchronous tool execution. Users perceive latency as intelligence. If the model calls 4 tools and you run them sequentially, you just 4x'd the user's wait time. Build a DAG executor or die." — 20-year engine dev, ex-Google/Anthropic

"The orphaned tool_use repair is a code smell that screams 'protocol violation upstream'. Either fix the model's tool-calling discipline or make the repair explicit and auditable. Silent mutation of history is how you get hallucinated tool results that poison the next turn." — Tools programmer, 15 years IDE/CLI work

"Config with 40 fields passed by reference to a 500-line function — that's not architecture, that's a hostage situation. Extract a TurnContext, an ExecutionPolicy, a ToolExecutor. The loop should know nothing about hooks, skills, or System One." — Architecture lead, shipped 3 AAA engines

"We shipped an MCP client in 2024. The stdio transport is fine for 2-3 servers. At 7 auto-starting? That's a fork bomb waiting for a user who installs Serena, Context7, and Playwright simultaneously. Where's the process pool?" — 20-year engine dev, ex-Blizzard

"Calling keyword overlap a 'decision model with 94% accuracy' is the kind of marketing that gets you sued when the guard tool misses a prompt injection. Ship the heuristic, call it a heuristic, benchmark it. Don't lie." — Tools programmer, ex-GitHub Copilot

"Two System One integrations? That's not a feature, that's a reorg that never finished. One team built the MCP server, another built the direct tools, nobody talked. The model sees 'systemone_classify' twice with different schemas. Good luck debugging that." — 15-year infra lead, ex-Stripe

"They built the castle walls (workspace sandbox, atomic writes, flock) but left the drawbridge down (pinning disabled, tokens unencrypted, shell injection). Classic 'security theater' — looks secure until you poke it." — Security engineer

"System One is the brain's safety layer — classification, verification, guard rails. But it talks to KEV over plaintext HTTP with zero pinning. That's not a safety layer, that's a backdoor with a neon sign." — Security engineer

"The MCP config ${VAR} expansion is a supply chain attack waiting to happen. One malicious .mcp.json in a shared repo and every developer's API keys walk out the front door. No signing, no trust-on-first-use, not even a warning." — Security engineer

"The Provider interface is Anthropic in a trench coat. Every new provider has to cosplay Anthropic's streaming deltas and cache_control quirks. That's not abstraction — that's a hostage situation." — 15-year infra lead, ex-Stripe
"Seven MCP servers auto-spawned on every launch? That's not a feature, that's a resource leak waiting for a user to file a bug about 'Pluto slow at startup'. Lazy init or GTFO." — Tools programmer

"I've seen this pattern before: a parallel AI system (System One) embedded in the main app with its own MCP server, config, and 20 tools. Six months from now the original authors leave and nobody dares touch it. It becomes the 'don't touch that module' legend." — 25-year veteran
"BFS attributes for session metadata is the most Haiku-native thing I've seen in years. Searchable in Tracker Find? Chef's kiss. That's platform integration done right." — Haiku kernel dev

"The hook system passes commands to /bin/sh -c after setenv. That's not 'safe' — that's 'we hope the config file isn't malicious'. Threat model: user edits their own config. But supply chain? Compromised dotfiles repo? One malicious hook_pre_tool and it's game over." — Security engineer

"Using private headers for a user-space app is asking for pain. We change those internals between beta releases. If Pluto ships on HaikuDepot, it'll break on the next update. Wrap BMessage/BLooper interfaces or accept the maintenance burden." — Haiku kernel dev

"The 1.5s snooze in the Tracker add-on is a classic rookie mistake. Tracker add-ons run in Tracker's thread — you're blocking the file manager. Launch the app asynchronously, register a BMessageFilter for B_REFS_RECEIVED." — Haiku app dev

"That space in 'Ask pluto' will haunt your packaging. hpkg handles it but every shell script in the build chain needs quotes. Rename it to ask-pluto. Also, your resource compilation uses four tools (rc/xres/resattr/addattr) — that's 3 too many." — Haiku Build Engineer

"System One as a built-in stdio MCP server is brilliant — zero config, auto-discovered. But StdioTransport::stop() has a zombie reaping bug: 50 * 10ms = 500ms wait after SIGKILL is too short for D-state processes. Use waitid(WEXITED) with no timeout." — Haiku kernel dev

"DesktopScriptTool is a loaded gun handed to the LLM. B_SET_PROPERTY and B_EXECUTE_PROPERTY on any running app? That's arbitrary code execution via scripting. At minimum, require user confirmation for write actions." — Haiku app dev

"Hardcoding /system/data/ssl/CARootCertificates.pem works today but Haiku may move to p11-kit or system cert store. Use BPath find_directory(B_SYSTEM_DATA_DIRECTORY) and append 'ssl/CARootCertificates.pem'." — Haiku Web+ Engineer

"21 test binaries, each with main() and custom CHECK macro? That's not a test suite, that's a collection of smoke tests. No fixtures, no parallel run, no XML output for CI. Invest in a tiny test framework (or adopt cpputest) — even a single header with TEST() macro and auto-registration would pay off in maintenance." — Haiku Build Engineer

"The BFS attribute integration is the kind of platform-deep thinking we did on console — make the OS do the indexing. But you've made the metadata *only* live there. One 'btrfs send' to a Linux box and it's gone. Consider a sidecar index." — 20-year engine dev

"Five implementations of atomic write. That's not DRY, that's 'each module owns its persistence'. Extract AtomicWrite(path, bytes, error) -> bool. One place to add fsync, one place to fix the rename-on-Windows edge case." — 15-year tools programmer

"OAuth tokens in plaintext at ~/config/settings/pluto/oauth-tokens? On a multi-user dev box? That's a 'how did this pass security review' finding. Haiku has no keychain, so encrypt with a per-user key derived from login password + machine ID." — Security engineer

"Global g_rag_mutex + g_wiki_mutex + g_entries vectors. You've reinvented the singleton anti-pattern. When (not if) someone wants project-scoped RAG *and* global RAG simultaneously, you'll be threading needles. Extract WorkspaceContext." — Architecture lead

"Frontmatter parser accepts 'tags: a, b, c' but not 'tags: [a, b, c]' or multiline. Users *will* copy YAML from the web and it'll silently break. Either use a real YAML parser (yaml-cpp, 1 header) or document the subset strictly." — Indie Dev

"Config migration runs once at startup with no rollback. If mkdir fails after rename, the user's config is gone. That's a 'ship stop' bug. Do: 1) copy to .new, 2) verify .new readable, 3) rename old→.bak, 4) rename .new→old. Atomic." — 20-year engine dev

"MainWindow.cpp is the largest single file I've seen in a production codebase since 2008. It's not 'big' - it's a liability. Split it. ChatView, ToolBlockManager, SlashCommandController, SessionManager, ModelPickerDialog, SettingsDialog, RoutineDialog, ScheduleDialog, WikiDialog, TelemetryDialog, AgentController. Use composition." — Engine Architect

"Provider abstraction leaking Anthropic concepts (cache_control, tool_use blocks) into the base interface? That's how you get locked into one vendor's streaming format. Define capabilities explicitly. Translate at boundaries." — Engine Architect

"Custom JSON parser with full Unicode surrogate handling and 256-depth limit? That's not NIH - that's control. nlohmann/json is 10k lines. Your json.h is 500. For a Haiku-only binary, that's the right call." — Indie Dev

"Routines + Schedules + Wiki as markdown with frontmatter + BFS attributes? That's a developer workspace that understands itself. The /wiki command saving to BFS-queryable files? Chef's kiss." — Toolsmith

"SSE SSRF protection that only validates the initial hostname? That's a CVE waiting for a redirect. curl follows 302s by default. Pin the IP at connect time, or use CURLOPT_RESOLVE to bypass DNS entirely for allowlisted hosts." — 20-year engine dev, ex-Google networking

"No retry on 429? In 2024? That's not a bug, that's a design decision to make users hate you during traffic spikes. Every provider returns 429 with retry-after. Parse it, back off, resume. The calc_backoff_ms function exists but is never called — that's the smell of code written but not integrated." — Tools programmer, ex-GitHub Copilot team

"Three SSE parsers in one codebase? That's not DRY, that's WET — Write Everything Thrice. When Anthropic changes their event format (and they will), you'll fix it in one place and the other two silently corrupt streams. Extract a shared SseParser class with unit tests, or accept that one will rot." — 25-year veteran, ex-Mozilla networking

"Placeholder pins in production? That's worse than no pinning — it's a false sense of security that delays real hardening. I've seen this exact pattern cause a 3-day outage when Let's Encrypt rotated and the pinned cert expired. Either operationalize pin rotation or delete the code." — 20-year engine dev, ex-Google networking
